A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same explanation-based GNN watermarking work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original node-classification experiments, pruning and fine-tuning evaluations, ablations, and MUTAG graph-classification results.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and adds dataset and architecture evaluations, baseline comparisons, robustness studies and training-time measurements.

M1.justification: The core watermark embedding and verification method remains unchanged, but Appendix E introduces an evaluated distillation-defense component: project the watermark through a private Gaussian matrix, perturb teacher logits, and train the student against the perturbed outputs using KL loss. V1 Appendix A.6 only proposed a different, unevaluated defense based on periodic distillation and a watermark-retention penalty.

E1.justification: V2 adds the large Reddit2 social-network dataset and evaluates CORA and CiteSeer in baseline comparisons. It also adds evaluation under Gaussian node-feature perturbations. MUTAG graph classification is retained and relocated to Appendix G; link prediction remains a proposed extension rather than an evaluated task.

E2.justification: V1 compares watermarked and ordinary models but does not experimentally compare competing watermarking methods. V2 adds evaluated comparisons with Xu et al. (2023) in Tables 9–10 and Shao et al. (2024) in Table 14. These methods were already cited in v1, but their participation in reported comparisons is new.

E3.justification: V2 adds Graph Transformer evaluations, a Reddit2-specific subgraph proportion of 0.03%, model-averaging and defended-distillation protocols, targeted trigger-removal testing, and feature-noise levels of 5%, 10% and 20%. New timing experiments use seven subgraphs and 256 hidden dimensions. The original 60/20/20 split and main 49-epoch fine-tuning procedure remain.

E4.justification: New analyses examine watermark survival after model merging, the proposed distillation defense, watermark-loss weight r, initialization stability, feature perturbations, targeted removal of Xu et al.'s triggers, and training overhead. Earlier subgraph-number, subgraph-size, architecture and learning-rate studies are retained. Distillation vulnerability itself was already reported in v1.

E5.justification: Five-trial averaging already appears in v1. V2 adds verification pass counts and dispersion reporting in Tables 9–13, including explicit means and standard deviations for stability tests. This does not establish increased run counts for retained experiments. The new distillation evaluation uses a 0.05 significance criterion despite the retained general verification threshold of 0.01.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial benchmark, comparator, robustness and runtime results. Table 9 reports 5/5 verification successes for the proposed method versus 4/5 for Xu et al. on CORA and PubMed; Table 6 reports defended-distillation p-values of 0.037 and 0.025. Retained Table 1 accuracy numbers receive reversed watermark/no-watermark labels, conflicting with v2 Table 8; this does not establish actual performance improvements.

T1.justification: Section 4.4 adds a short reduction sketch from Maximum k-Subset Intersection to finding subgraphs with maximally matching explanations. V1 provided combinatorial search-space counts without this reduction argument. The existing kernel definitions, watermark-design derivations and asymptotic complexity analysis are retained.

C1.justification: The headline contributions remain explanation-based GNN watermarking without training-data manipulation, black-box verification using statistically distinctive explanations, NP-hard watermark location, and robustness to pruning and fine-tuning. The additional appendix mechanism and experiments do not substantively redefine the abstract and introduction's contribution list.

C2.justification: V2 adds mechanism explanations for watermark transfer through perturbed teacher outputs, trigger detectability in backdoor watermarking, and limitations of adapting Shao et al.'s approach to graphs. It also adds practical complexity interpretations and qualifications concerning Reddit2 convergence and computationally restricted ablations. These extend the interpretation and applicability discussion beyond v1.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-access link and substantial implementation information for new experiments: Xu et al.'s reimplementation and poisoning settings, PCA/K-Means trigger detection and relabeling, feature-noise construction, and timing configurations. Dataset statistics and measured training times are added. The original hardware description and general training hyperparameter ranges remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations covering maximum subset intersection, model merging, GraphSAINT, Graph Transformer, FedGMark and broader GNN research. Appendix F gives more specific distinctions from Xu et al. and Shao et al. The central positioning as the first explanation-based GNN watermarking method remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Much of the abstract, introduction, related work and methodological prose is rewritten and condensed. The appendix is reorganized from A.1–A.6 into sections A–H, graph-task extensions move out of the main text, and ablations become nested within results. Authorship, disclosures and reproducibility sections also change.

P2.justification: Table 1 is redesigned into separate accuracy and watermark panels with a Transformer column. Figures 2–3 gain Reddit2 panels, Figure 2 changes from stacked to side-by-side presentation, and Figures 4–5 are enlarged. Numerous new experimental tables are introduced, while algorithms are reformatted and relocated.

improvement.justification: Direct baseline comparisons, stability tests, uncertainty reporting and implementation information improve the paper's empirical assessability relative to v1. However, new reporting problems limit these gains: Table 1 reverses retained accuracy labels, and the distillation results presented as successful verification have p-values of 0.025 and 0.037, exceeding the stated default threshold of 0.01. The added evidence supports a limited overall improvement despite these unresolved inconsistencies.
